result:
I've fixed the search index so it follows your rule through archiving, restoring, new comments and issue edits, and in the rebuild job. The full suite passes (617 tests, typecheck and lint clean). A throwaway test in /tmp also passed: it covered all four support reports, 130+ issues and one issue with 120 comments in a single workspace, and a second workspace left alone. I've deleted it, so no new tests were added to the repo.

- **One place decides what's searchable** (`search-service.ts`). The issue, comment and project index functions now check the live chain themselves (comment → issue → project). If the chain is live the entry is written; if not, it's removed. Previously they indexed whatever they were given.
- **Archiving and restoring cascade.** Archiving an issue now removes its comments too. Archiving or restoring a project re-checks the project, every issue in it and every comment on those issues. So archiving hides everything underneath whether or not the admin archived the issues. Restoring brings back only issues and comments that are still live. Issues archived with the project or before it, and deleted comments, stay hidden.
- **New activity is checked too.** Comments and issue edits made later on kept issues in an archived project are checked against the rule, so they stay hidden. Manual "reindex this item" requests now work for projects and comments as well as issues. Before, they only handled issues.
- **The rebuild job** (`search-reindex-job.ts`):
  - It now reads every page of projects, issues and comments. Before, it stopped after the first 100 of each, which is why older issues went missing in large workspaces.
  - It no longer re-adds archived content.
  - It finishes by deleting every entry in that workspace's index that the rule doesn't allow. That covers leftover or duplicate entries and entries for items that no longer exist.
  - Everything it reads and deletes is limited to the one workspace.

Two small helpers support this: `forEachInPages` in `src/lib/pagination.ts` walks every page of a listing, and `pruneSearchDocuments` in `search-repository.ts` does the final clean-up.

Things I didn't change:
- Search results still come straight from the index; there's no extra liveness check when a search runs. Correct results depend on the event listeners being registered, which the app does at startup. Anything that changes the database without going through the services will leave the index out of date until a rebuild.
- Editing a comment or a project's name or description still doesn't update its search text. That was already the case and wasn't in the support reports.
